body.purpose: Reading copy and every heading, including the hero <h1>: sector summary, hero subhead, section titles, news headlines, stock blurbs, the modal's article summary. Self-hosted Montserrat (user-supplied, replaced General Sans). A Cormorant Garamond serif was tried for the hero H1 after studying cluely.com, then reverted at the user's explicit request — the page stays strictly two-voice, no serif exception.

label.purpose: Every number, ticker, timestamp, and uppercase short label. Self-hosted Azeret Mono (slashed zero), not the OS system monospace. Doubles as the tabular-nums numeric voice.

shadows.name: modal-float
shadows.purpose: Both modals (News, Stock Detail) — heavier than the toast because they sit over a dark scrim.

shadows.name: live-status-halo
shadows.purpose: Soft ring around the live-status dot when data.json is real, not demo.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for hover/focus/active state changes on buttons, chips, rows, inputs.

motion.name: ticker-scroll
motion.purpose: Continuous, calm ticker-tape scroll; pauses on hover; disabled (falls back to manual overflow-x scroll) under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The only button variant in use (e.g. 'Instalar app'). Pill radius, transparent fill, navy on hover.

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Default (unselected) filter chip. Monospace uppercase label, transparent fill.

components.name: Filter Chip — Active
components.description: Selected filter chip. The only place a chip becomes a filled solid-navy surface.

components.name: Sentiment Badge
components.description: Pill badge at ~8-10% tint of the semantic color; used for sector sentiment, per-stock tags, and news dots. bullish/bearish/mixed modifiers shown. Each modifier also carries a small trend glyph (diagonal arrow up/down, or a short wave for mixed) via mask-image + currentColor, drawn in the same stroke language as the page's sparklines/charts. Added as the project's one deliberate finance-iconography touch, inspired by how broker sites like invertironline signal money context visually, without adopting their color palette or illustration style.
components.html: Alcista
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.63rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 3px 8px; border-radius: 999px; } .ds-badge::before { content: ''; width: 9px; height: 9px; flex-shrink: 0; background-color: currentColor; mask-repeat: no-repeat; mask-position: center; mask-size: contain; } .ds-badge--bullish { color: var(--rise, #2e7d4f); background: rgba(46,125,79,0.1); } .ds-badge--bearish { color: var(--fall, #9e3a2f); background: rgba(158,58,47,0.1); } .ds-badge--mixed { color: var(--mixed, #5b6b7a); background: rgba(91,107,122,0.1); } .ds-badge--bullish::before { mask-image: var(--icon-trend-up); } .ds-badge--bearish::before { mask-image: var(--icon-trend-down); } .ds-badge--mixed::before { mask-image: var(--icon-trend-mixed); }

components.name: Stat Block
components.description: The one reusable way to show 2-6 labeled numbers side by side: monospace tabular-nums value stacked over a small faint label, in a repeat(3,1fr) grid with a hairline top border. Used for the sector hero's up-count/avg-change/news-count and the Stock Detail Modal's fundamentals (P/E, market cap, 52-week range, EPS, ROE, net margin). Missing data renders as a muted 'N/D', never a fabricated number.

components.css: .ds-stat-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 16px 10px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); padding-top: 18px; } .ds-stat { text-align: left; } .ds-stat-value { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text, #101828); } .ds-stat-value--na { color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); font-weight: 500; } .ds-stat-label { font-size: 0.7rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); margin-top: 3px; }

components.name: Fundamentals Glossary
components.description: Collapsible plain-language glossary for the Stat Block's fundamentals, collapsed by default under a text-only toggle. Contextual by design: explains P/E, market cap, 52-week range, EPS, ROE and net margin right where a visitor is already looking at them, instead of a permanent page-level panel that would be noise for visitors who already know the terms.

components.css: .ds-help-toggle { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 0; border: none; background: transparent; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); cursor: pointer; } .ds-help-toggle:hover { color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); } .ds-help-chevron { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.9em; transition: transform 0.12s ease; } .ds-help-toggle[aria-expanded="true"] .ds-help-chevron { transform: rotate(180deg); } .ds-help-panel { border-top: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); } .ds-help-item { padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); } .ds-help-item dt { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text, #101828); margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-help-item dd { font-size: 0.82rem; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); margin: 0; }

components.name: Ledger Row
components.description: Signature component. One row of the stock table: ticker/name/blurb, tabular-nums price and change, sparkline, sentiment tag — sharing a fixed column grid with the table header. Clickable, opens the Stock Detail Modal.

components.css: .ds-ledger-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(150px,1.6fr) 70px 60px 90px 80px; gap: 16px; align-items: center; padding: 18px 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease; } .ds-ledger-row:hover { background: var(--panel-raised, #eef1f5); } .ds-ledger-id { display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-ledger-ticker { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.95rem; } .ds-ledger-name { font-size: 0.76rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); } .ds-ledger-price { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 600; text-align: right; } .ds-ledger-change { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 600; text-align: right; } .ds-ledger-change--down { color: var(--fall, #9e3a2f); } .ds-ledger-spark { width: 100%; height: 36px; } .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.63rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 3px 8px; border-radius: 999px; } .ds-badge--bearish { color: var(--fall, #9e3a2f); background: rgba(158,58,47,0.1); }

components.name: Sortable Ledger Header
components.description: Empresa/Precio/Var. column headers are real buttons that sort the ledger ascending/descending; Tendencia and Señal stay plain labels since a sparkline or sentiment pill isn't meaningfully sortable. Active column turns accent-navy with a small triangle glyph and gets aria-sort; numeric columns default to descending (biggest first), name defaults ascending (A-Z).
components.css: .ds-ledger-sort { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.66rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); background: none; border: none; padding: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-ledger-sort[aria-sort] { color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); }

components.name: Watchlist Star
components.description: Small star button at the start of each ledger row, toggling a locally-persisted (localStorage, no account) favorite. Unfilled outline at rest, fills solid accent-navy once starred, matching the 'active state = accent' language already used for the active filter chip. Click is stopped from bubbling so it never opens the Stock Detail Modal. Powers a fifth filter chip, '★ Favoritas'.
components.html: <button class="ds-stock-star active" aria-pressed="true" aria-label="Quitar de favoritas"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor"><path d="M8 1.6l1.87 3.98 4.33.5-3.23 3.02.9 4.4L8 11.35l-3.87 2.15.9-4.4-3.23-3.02 4.33-.5L8 1.6Z"/></svg></button>

components.name: List Toggle
components.description: Shared 'Ver más'/'Ver menos' collapse control for the ledger (21 stocks) and the news list (8 items) — both load showing only the first 3 entries so the page doesn't dump everything on load. Full-width monospace text button, hairline-separated from the last row. Switching the active filter chip or typing in search resets the ledger back to collapsed; sorting does not.
components.html: <button type="button" class="ds-list-toggle">Ver 18 más</button>
components.css: .ds-list-toggle { display: block; width: 100%; margin: 4px 0 0; padding: 14px 4px; border: none; border-top: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); background: transparent; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); text-align: center; cursor: pointer; } .ds-list-toggle:hover { color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); background: var(--panel-raised, #eef1f5); }

components.name: News Row
components.description: One row of the news list: rounded-square status dot, headline + source/time meta, bracketed monospace ticker tag. The whole row is clickable/focusable and opens the News Modal — it never navigates away on its own.

components.css: .ds-news-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: 14px; padding: 16px 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease; } .ds-news-row:hover, .ds-news-row:focus-visible { background: var(--panel-raised, #eef1f5); } .ds-news-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-news-dot--up { background: var(--rise, #2e7d4f); } .ds-news-dot--down { background: var(--fall, #9e3a2f); } .ds-news-body { min-width: 0; } .ds-news-headline { font-size: 0.92rem; font-weight: 500; margin: 0 0 4px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-news-meta { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); } .ds-news-tag { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Earnings Calendar Grid
components.description: Forward-looking month-grid calendar of upcoming quarterly earnings dates for tracked tickers (Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALENDAR, filtered locally, next ~3 months). Replaced an earlier flat list-with-month-dividers at the user's request for more visual dynamism. One month at a time with prev/next nav; can't navigate before the current month (no historical data behind this section). Days with a report get an accent-tinted cell and a small clickable ticker pill; clicking opens the Stock Detail Modal. Real earnings dates only, deliberately not 'important events' (no reliable API for that). Whole section self-hides when there's no upcoming data at all.

components.css: .ds-cal-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 18px; margin-bottom: 14px; } .ds-cal-month { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-cal-nav { width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, #ccd3dc); background: transparent; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); cursor: pointer; } .ds-cal-weekdays { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr); margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-cal-weekdays span { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); text-align: center; } .ds-cal-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr); gap: 3px; } .ds-cal-cell { min-height: 54px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); padding: 5px 4px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-cal-day { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.66rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); } .ds-has-entry { background: var(--accent-dim, rgba(28,58,94,.08)); border-color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); } .ds-cal-entry { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.6rem; font-weight: 700; padding: 2px 5px; border-radius: 4px; border: none; background: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); color: var(--panel, #fff); cursor: pointer; }

components.css: .ds-modal-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 24px; } .ds-modal-panel { position: relative; background: var(--panel, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); border-top: 2px solid var(--accent, #1c3a5e); border-radius: 4px; padding: 32px 28px 28px; max-width: 520px; width: 100%; max-height: 85vh; overflow-y: auto; box-shadow: 0 20px 50px -16px rgba(16,24,40,0.4); } .ds-modal-close { position: absolute; top: 14px; right: 14px; width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, #ccd3dc); background: transparent; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); font-size: 1.1rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-modal-ticker { display: inline-block; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); margin-bottom: 10px; } .ds-modal-headline { font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; margin: 0 0 8px; padding-right: 28px; } .ds-modal-meta { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); margin: 0 0 18px; } .ds-modal-summary { font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text, #101828); margin: 0 0 22px; } .ds-modal-link { font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--accent-dim, rgba(28,58,94,0.08)); }

components.name: Stock Detail Modal
components.description: Signature component. Opens when a Ledger Row is clicked: large price/change, an enlarged price chart, a Stat Block of fundamentals (P/E, market cap, 52-week range, EPS, ROE, net margin), and a related-news list scoped to that ticker — each item swaps this modal for the News Modal. Wider than the News Modal (600px) to fit the chart. The chart renders real OHLC candlesticks once daily_ohlc.json has data for that ticker; otherwise it falls back to the line-chart built from hourly snapshots, with the caption always stating which one is showing.

components.css: .ds-stock-ticker { display: block; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.15rem; color: var(--text, #101828); } .ds-stock-name { font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); } .ds-price-value { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.3rem; color: var(--text, #101828); } .ds-price-change { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; } .ds-price-change--down { color: var(--fall, #9e3a2f); } .ds-stock-chart { width: 100%; height: 180px; margin: 20px 0 8px; } .ds-chart-caption { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); margin: 0 0 26px; } .ds-related-title { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); margin: 0 0 10px; } .ds-related-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; width: 100%; padding: 12px 4px; border: none; border-top: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); background: transparent; font: inherit; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; } .ds-related-item:hover { background: var(--panel-raised, #eef1f5); }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: The one text input in the system. Sharp 4px radius (input language, not pill language).
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="search" placeholder="Buscar empresa o ticker…">

components.name: Ticker Tape Item
components.description: Signature component. One symbol/price/change entry in the continuously scrolling ticker tape, separated by hairline rules.
components.html: NVDA$219.11-2.2%
components.css: .ds-ticker-item { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 9px; padding: 11px 24px; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; border-right: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e6ec); color: var(--text-dim, #475467); } .ds-ticker-symbol { color: var(--text, #101828); font-weight: 700; } .ds-ticker-change--up { color: var(--rise, #2e7d4f); } .ds-ticker-change--down { color: var(--fall, #9e3a2f); }

components.name: Preloader
components.description: Fixed full-viewport brand moment shown from the HTML before app.js paints anything, covering the empty-shell flash while init() fetches data.json. Removed once real content is ready (not on a fixed timer), with window 'load' as a safety net and a 250ms minimum display floor. Reuses the topbar's exact wordmark markup so the brand identity is continuous, not a separate asset.
components.html: AI Stocks Pulse
components.css: #preloader { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 9999; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 14px; background: var(--paper, #f7f8fa); transition: opacity 0.4s ease; } #preloader.hidden { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; } .ds-preloader-logo { width: 40px; height: 40px; animation: preloader-pulse 1.4s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-preloader-name { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--text-dim, #475467); } .ds-preloader-name strong { color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); font-weight: 700; } @keyframes preloader-pulse { 0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 0.7; } 50% { transform: scale(1.08); opacity: 1; } }

components.name: Market Status Pill
components.description: Credibility detail in the topbar: 'Mercado abierto'/'Mercado cerrado' for NYSE/Nasdaq regular hours (9:30-16:00 America/New_York, weekdays), computed via Intl.DateTimeFormat (handles DST correctly) and refreshed every 60s client-side without a reload. Same visual recipe as the demo/live pill beside it (hairline border, leading dot, rise-green + halo when open) so both read as one status-indicator family. Known simplification: no market-holiday calendar. Hidden under 640px alongside the demo/live pill.
components.html: Mercado abierto
components.css: .ds-market-status { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.65rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 10px 6px 8px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, #ccd3dc); color: var(--text-dim, #475467); } .ds-market-status::before { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--text-faint, #98a2b3); } .ds-market-status.open { color: var(--rise, #2e7d4f); border-color: rgba(47,122,79,0.35); } .ds-market-status.open::before { background: var(--rise, #2e7d4f); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--rise-dim, rgba(46,125,79,0.1)); }

components.name: Category Icon
components.description: 16px hand-rolled line icon, colored by concept (Navy for time/pulse, Teal for company/structure, Indigo for ratios and news, Green for dollar-value figures) rather than the page's single accent. A deliberate, user-requested exception to the One Accent Rule, inspired by invertironline's per-category icon coloring but built as our own restrained icon set instead of adopting their illustration style or palette. Appears in section headers, hero stats, and the Stock Detail Modal's fundamentals grid, reusing the same icon+color pairing wherever the same concept recurs.
components.html: Empresas del sector
components.css: .icon-glyph { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex-shrink: 0; vertical-align: -3px; } .icon-navy { color: var(--accent, #1c3a5e); } .icon-teal { color: var(--icon-teal, #1f7a72); } .icon-indigo { color: var(--icon-indigo, #4a5a8f); } .icon-green { color: var(--rise, #2e7d4f); }

components.name: Hero Mover
components.description: Real-data replacement for a rejected illustrated-asset attempt: the sector's top gainer and top loser, computed client-side from STOCKS, filling the hero-text column's remaining space below the badges. Reuses the existing stock-tag pill (ticker + trend glyph) rather than a new pill style. Each one is a real button that opens the Stock Detail Modal for that ticker, same as clicking its ledger row.

components.name: Composite Chart Range Toggle
components.description: Segmented control (Hoy / 30 días / 60 días) above the hero's composite sector chart. "Hoy" resamples the short hourly price-snapshot window; the two longer ranges resample real daily closes across every tracked ticker. Deliberately stops at 60 días — the pipeline only keeps 60 days of daily candles, so a 90-day option would promise history the product doesn't have. Reuses the Chip visual language at a smaller size rather than inventing a second toggle style.

components.name: Composite Sector Chart
components.description: The hero's equal-weighted % sector index chart, redesigned via the taste-skill's anti-slop review after the user called the original plain polyline+flat-fill version 'horrible'. Redesign-Preserve: reuses this project's own existing tokens rather than a foreign visual language. Smooth Catmull-Rom curve instead of straight segments; real vertical gradient fill (same semantic rise/fall hue, 30%-to-0% opacity) instead of flat opacity; endpoint dot reuses the project's existing 'live-status halo' ring recipe (--rise-dim/--fall-dim); small muted monospace date labels at both bottom corners for axis context; interactive crosshair + fixed-position tooltip on hover/touch showing the exact date and % return at any point on the curve (previously only the final value was readable). Motion is interaction-driven only, no ambient animation.

components.name: Watchlist Position
components.description: "Mi posición" panel in the Stock Detail Modal, between the sentiment tag and the chart. Gated behind the ticker already being favorited (the star is the declared "I care about this" signal). Empty state is a purchase-price input plus an optional share-count input; filled state shows the total hypothetical gain/loss ($ and %, when share count is set) and current position value, in the same up/down color and tabular-nums voice used everywhere else, plus a plain-text clear control. Both fields live only in localStorage (aisp_cost_basis, {price, shares} per ticker) — never sent to any server.

narrative.overview:
A calm, considered instrument for reading the AI stocks sector. This palette went through four directions before landing here: a black terminal (too generic-AI-dashboard), sage-green ledger paper (too "eco," didn't read as financial), a parchment-and-gold stock-certificate motif (distinctive, but more editorial than "commonly used and comfortable") — and settled on the colors people already recognize from finance software itself: a cool neutral white/grey base with a single navy-blue accent, the convention most banking and trading apps actually use. One accent, everywhere, per the Lila Rule.

The system is deliberately single-theme (light only). This is a daily-use tool, not a themeable brand site — committing to one world was a conscious choice, not an omission.
keyCharacteristics: Cool neutral white/light-grey background, the convention of banking and trading software
One accent only: navy blue, used identically everywhere
A separate, distinct semantic triad (green/red/slate) for rise/fall/mixed — never reuses the accent hue
Two deliberate type voices: a plain sans for reading, a tracked-out monospace for every number and label
Flat surfaces, hairline dividers, real data visualizations instead of decorative imagery
Reading an article's summary happens in place (a modal), never an automatic redirect off the page

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ledger Navy is the only brand accent on text, badges, borders, and surfaces, full stop. It never does semantic work — if a color means rise/fall/mixed, it is never navy. The one narrow exception: the Category Icon set (Teal, Indigo, plus reused Navy/Green) colors small 16px icon glyphs only, never anything else.

rules.name: The No-Black Rule
rules.body: No #000000 and no clinical, context-free #ffffff — panels and text both carry a deliberate cool bias rather than being pure values.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: If it's read, it's the sans. If it's a number, a ticker, or a short label, it's the tracked-out monospace. Never mix the two within a single value. No exceptions - a Cormorant Garamond serif hero was tried and reverted at the user's request.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Elevation is earned only by things that are genuinely temporary or floating above the page (the toast, the two modals). A permanent, in-flow element never gets a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: If it's something you click or a status you read, it's a pill (999px). If it's something you read data or an article inside of, it's 4px. No third radius.

dos: Do keep Ledger Navy as the only accent, used identically everywhere.
Do run every number, ticker, and short label through the monospace label voice with tabular-nums; keep sentences in the sans.
Do use hairlines and tonal shifts for hierarchy and depth; reach for a shadow only for the toast and the two modals.
Do apply the pill radius to anything clickable or status-bearing, and the 4px radius to anything you read data or an article inside of — no other radius value.
Do let a visitor read an article summary in place (the modal) rather than redirecting them off the page by default; the external link stays available but explicit.
Do treat real data (sparklines, the composite chart, the ticker tape) as the page's visual anchor instead of decorative imagery.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color, warm-tinted neutrals, or a dark mode — this cool-neutral, single-navy-accent palette is a deliberate commitment made after three prior directions were tried and moved away from.
Don't add drop shadows to permanent in-flow elements (cards, rows, panels) — only the toast and the two modals get one.
Don't default to rounded-lg (8-16px) cards; the system has exactly two radii and both are already assigned.
Don't reach for a three-equal-column card grid for the stock list — it's a ledger table with a shared column grid, not a card grid.
Don't add gradients, glows, or glossy/3D abstract imagery — explicitly tried and rejected during this project for reading as generic AI-generated art.
Don't make a news row (or any link out of the page) navigate automatically on click — the summary appears in place first; leaving the page is the visitor's explicit next choice.
